steps.text: In real life, conduction, convection, and radiation often happen together. Let's pick them apart.
Tap a method — start with “Conduction” — to see where it's happening.
Take boiling water on a stove: the pot heats by conduction, the water circulates by convection, and you feel radiation from the flame — all at once.
Conduction (through solids), convection (in fluids), radiation (as rays). Most everyday heating uses more than one of them together.

coach.mission: Spot conduction, convection, and radiation working together.
whenStuck: Tap each method to see where it happens in the scene.
Solid → conduction, fluid → convection, rays → radiation.
whenWrong: Conduction is through solids, convection is in fluids, radiation is rays.
In one scene, all three can be happening at the same time.
whenCorrect: Right — that's the correct method for that part of the scene.
Good — real heating usually combines all three.
coach.done: You've seen all three heat-transfer methods work together. Move on when you're ready.
